summary: Gross margin 54.4% (2023), 56.1% (2024), 59.9% (2025). Operating margin 42.6%, 45.7%, 50.8%. Net margin 39.4%, 40.0%, 44.5%. Revenue over the same period NT$2,161,736M, NT$2,894,308M, NT$3,809,054M — up 76% cumulatively.
analyst_note: THE CENTRAL FACT OF THIS ANALYSIS. Margins expanded while volume grew 76%. Growth bought with price or subsidy compresses margin; this does the opposite. It is the clearest differentiator versus 005930, whose margin surge came from a +220% memory ASP spike — a rent, not a position.

summary: Advanced technologies (7nm and below) were 58% of wafer revenue in 2023, 69% in 2024 and 74% in 2025 (77% by Q2 2026). 2025 detail: 3nm 24%, 5nm 36%, 7nm 14%. 2-nanometer entered VOLUME PRODUCTION in 2025; 16-angstrom development on track with risk production expected in 2026.
analyst_note: The node lead is extending rather than being defended. Combined with 2nm booked into 2028 and CoWoS sold out, this is forward visibility that only a widening moat produces.

summary: FY2025 net revenue NT$3,809,054M (US$121,423M), +31.6% YoY; gross profit NT$2,281,294M; income from operations NT$1,936,092M (US$61,718M); net income to parent NT$1,697,604M (US$54,116M). R&D NT$246,427M (US$7,855M), 6.5% of revenue versus 7.1% in 2024 and 8.5% in 2023.
analyst_note: R&D rising in absolute terms every year while falling as a share of revenue is operating leverage on the moat itself.

summary: HPC platform revenue NT$934,769M (43% of total, 2023), NT$1,476,891M (51%, 2024), NT$2,192,931M (58%, 2025) — +48% YoY in 2025. Smartphone fell from 38% to 29%. North America revenue rose from 68% to 75% of total; China fell from 12% to 9%.
analyst_note: The mix shift to AI compute is complete and measured, but it also means the revenue base is increasingly a derivative of one end market and one geography.

summary: Capex NT$949,817M (2023), NT$956,007M (2024), NT$1,272,411M / US$40,895M (2025) — 44.0%, 33.0% and 33.4% of revenue. FY2026 guidance is US$52-56 billion, a 27-37% step-up, focused on 2nm/3nm capacity (Fabs 20, 21, 22), specialty and advanced packaging (Fab 24), and R&D. D&A was NT$688,096M in 2025.
analyst_note: THE STRUCTURAL LIMITATION. TSMC must spend roughly a third of revenue every year to hold its position — the opposite of NVDA's 2.8%-of-revenue model. Free cash flow was only US$31.6B on US$121.4B of revenue. The offsetting positive is that incremental ROIC is RISING: margins expanded 8.2pp over two years while capital intensity stayed flat.

summary: Cash, cash equivalents and current marketable securities NT$3,068,595M (US$97,820M) at 2025-12-31, up from NT$2,422,019M. Short-term loans NIL. Aggregate long-term debt NT$1,032,988M (US$32,929M) at fixed rates of 0.41%-4.63% with maturities to 35 years. Net cash approximately US$64.9B. Operating cash flow US$72,521M in 2025.
analyst_note: 2025 capex was funded against only NT$86,900M of bond issuance — roughly 93% from operating cash flow. Financial survivability is not the risk here; the risk is physical and geopolitical.

summary: Ten largest customers accounted for 70% (2023), 76% (2024) and 78% (2025) of net revenue. Largest customer 25%, 22%, 19%. Second largest 11%, 12%, 17%.
analyst_note: The moat is increasingly rented to fewer tenants. Note the divergence: the largest customer is shrinking as a share while the second is rising fast — consistent with a smartphone-to-AI mix shift within the customer base. Less severe than NVDA's 12%-to-22% single-customer jump, but the same direction.

summary: Fab footprint: nine fabs in Hsinchu Science Park, two in Central Taiwan Science Park, seven in Southern Taiwan Science Park, Fab 22 in Kaohsiung; overseas Fab 11 (Washington), Fab 21 (Arizona), Fab 23 (Kumamoto), Fab 24 (Dresden, under construction), Fab 10 (Shanghai), Fab 16 (Nanjing). Taiwan fab land is LEASED from science-park administrations, with Kaohsiung Fab 22 leases up for renewal by December 2026 and some Southern Taiwan leases from March 2026.
analyst_note: THE DEFINING RISK OF THIS POSITION, and the reason asymmetry scores 4/10 rather than 5. Unlike 005930 (cycle) or NVDA (demand), TSMC's tail is a genuine loss of the asset base. It is UNRESEARCHABLE — no analysis converts geopolitical probability into a measurement — so it must be SIZED rather than resolved.

summary: TSMC Arizona entered agreements with the US Department of Commerce in November 2024 for up to US$6.6B in direct CHIPS Act funding plus up to US$5B in loans; TSMC provided an 'irrevocable, absolute and unconditional guarantee' of TSMC Arizona's obligations to the DOC. ESMC (Dresden) agreed up to EUR5B of German state aid in December 2024. Incentives carry compliance, milestone and clawback conditions, plus restrictions on expansion in foreign countries of concern.
analyst_note: Genuinely two-sided. The subsidies materially de-risk overseas expansion, but the parent guarantee is full recourse and the conditions constrain future strategic freedom.

summary: Overseas subsidiaries are structured with customer-partners sharing capital and risk: JASM (Kumamoto) is 72.6% TSMC-owned with Sony, DENSO and Toyota as minorities; ESMC (Dresden) is 70.0% TSMC-owned with Bosch, Infineon and NXP each holding 10%. Quarterly dividend raised from NT$5.00 to NT$6.00 per share during 2025, approximately NT$570.5B declared for the year.
analyst_note: Best capital-allocation record among the three companies analysed in this harness: ~93% self-funded capex, nil short-term debt, partner-shared overseas risk, and a 20% dividend increase in the same year as record capex. Offset only by the absence of buybacks.

summary: January-July 2026 revenue NT$2,872,060M, +37.0% YoY; July 2026 alone NT$467,580M, +44.7% YoY and +5.6% MoM. Company guidance is FY2026 revenue growth slightly above +40% YoY in USD. Advanced nodes reached 77% of wafer revenue in Q2 2026. 2nm capacity booked well into 2028; CoWoS sold out through the ramp from roughly 75-80k to 120-130k wafers per month.
source: TSMC monthly revenue disclosures (Form 6-K) and company IR — tier-2
analyst_note: Forward visibility here is materially better than for either 005930 or NVDA. It is the main reason expectation_gap scores 9/15 rather than NVDA's 8 despite a higher trailing multiple.

summary: ADS close US$414.00 on 2026-09-01. At 25,932,524,521 common shares and a 1:5 ADS ratio (5,186.5M ADS), market capitalisation is US$2,147B; less US$64.9B net cash, enterprise value is US$2,082B. Trailing P/E 39.7x on FY2025 EPS of US$10.43 per ADS; trailing EV/EBIT 33.7x; trailing FCF yield 1.47%.
source: Market price (tier-4 aggregator) combined with tier-1 share count from the 20-F
analyst_note: SOURCE CONFLICT RESOLVED: aggregators reported both US$1.93T and US$2.15-2.16T market cap. Computing from the tier-1 share count confirms US$2,147B; the US$1.93T quote is stale or wrong. The ADS price is the ONLY non-primary input in this valuation.

summary: Form SD for CY2025 filed 2026-05-26 with a Conflict Minerals Report describing a reasonable country-of-origin inquiry and a due-diligence framework across tantalum, tin, tungsten and gold, built on TSMC's Ethics and Business policies and supplier requirements.
source: TSMC Form SD CY2025, SEC — tier-1
analyst_note: Low analytical weight, recorded for completeness since the document was supplied. A governance positive with no red flags; it does not move any category score.

summary: 기업 품질은 유지하지만 기존 기대수익률 5년 연 6.6%는 미국 9% 요구수익률보다 낮다. 연구로 없앨 수 없는 대만 위험이라는 이유만으로 낮은 보상에도 STARTER를 정당화할 수 없다. 76점 WATCH로 조정한다.
analyst_note: 과거 충돌 주장은 삭제하지 않고 역사로 보존. 현행 판단은 동일 날짜 재평가 오버레이가 우선한다.
